title: Lifting equivariant vector-space diagrams to the point Weil heart
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $g_s$ be geometric Frobenius. Fix a finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use the raw constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], Weil pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], the specified point-fibre functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and point transport $\iota_N:\operatorname{Fib}_sN\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lg_s^*N)$ [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Write $\omega_E=H^0\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$, with degree-zero cohomology of [def-weil-coefficient-cohomology-modules].
Let $I$ be a finite category, let $D:I\to\mathrm{Vect}_{E,\mathrm{fd}}$ be a diagram, and give each $D(i)$ an automorphism $A_i$ such that $D(u)A_i=A_jD(u)$ for every arrow $u:i\to j$. One may designate finitely many short exact sequences among its arrows. Suppose at a chosen object $i_*$ an $E$-Weil heart object $(M_*,\theta_*)$ and a fibre isomorphism $\eta_*:\omega_E(M_*)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(i_*)$ are prescribed, satisfying $\eta_*\omega_E(\theta_*)H^0(\iota_{M_*})\eta_*^{-1}=A_{i_*}$.
There are a diagram of constructible $E$-Weil sheaves $(M_i,\theta_i)$ and specified fibre isomorphisms $\eta_i:\omega_E(M_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(i)$ realizing the entire given diagram. The object and fibre isomorphism at $i_*$ are exactly the prescribed ones. All diagram equations hold, each designated sequence is short exact in the underlying heart, and monomorphisms and cokernels in the vector diagram are realized as such in that heart. Under the degree-zero fibre identifications the lifted Weil map is characterized by
$$\omega_E(\theta_i)=\eta_i^{-1}A_i\eta_i\,H^0(\iota_{M_i})^{-1},\qquad
\omega_E(\widetilde D(u))=\eta_j^{-1}D(u)\eta_i.$$
Its inverse realizes the inverse linear map. In particular every lifted arrow satisfies $\widetilde D(u)\theta_i=\theta_j Lg_s^*\widetilde D(u)$. The local Frobenius operator [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] on each fibre is exactly $A_i$ under $\eta_i$. All objects, arrows and inverse Weil maps are over the same $E$. Their common-stage images over $\Omega$ realize the scalar-extended diagram, retain its exact sequences and the prescribed object, and use the specified scalar and point-transport comparisons. These assertions hold for every finite-field datum and impose no continuity or semisimplicity on the $A_i$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-point-equivariant-original-diagram] to obtain the original-field diagram, exact realization, specified transport, forward Weil-map formula and literal prescribed data.

For each i, equality of the forward homs identifies omega(theta_i) as the iso t_i.symm followed by eta_i, A_i and eta_i.symm. Taking inverses gives exactly the required inverse formula. Substitute the forward formula into eta_i.inv ≫ t_i.hom ≫ omega(theta_i).hom ≫ eta_i.hom; cancel t_i.hom ≫ t_i.inv, eta_i.inv ≫ eta_i.hom and eta_i.hom ≫ eta_i.inv to obtain A_i.hom. This completes ZlPointDiagramRealization.

For every finite overfield L of F, apply [lem-zl-point-equivariant-finite-scalar] to this same realized diagram and the recorded coefficientInclusion F L. Apply [lem-zl-point-equivariant-common-stage] to include this diagram at the original stage F. Assemble their conclusions with the original-field and prescribed-data assertions.
